content.title: About
content.content: Soft pretzels are a yeast‑leavened baked snack that is flash‑frozen right after shaping and baking, then coated with grated cheese. After thawing they retain a tender, slightly chewy texture and a rich melted‑cheese flavor. They are convenient to store in the freezer and can be quickly prepared in an oven or microwave.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Soft pretzels originated in Germany, where they are called "Brezel".
The classic twisted shape historically symbolized crossed arms, a medieval sign of blessing.
Freezing locks in the freshness and aroma of the cheese longer than fresh‑baked pretzels.
The cheese topping is often a blend of cheddar and parmesan, giving a sharp, savory taste.
In the United States soft pretzels are frequently served with mustard or honey dip.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: The cheese topping provides high‑quality dairy protein important for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Calcium
items.content: Hard cheeses are rich in calcium, supporting bone and tooth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Yeast‑based dough contains B1, B2 and B6 vitamins that aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Quick energy
items.content: The pretzel dough supplies carbohydrates that give a fast source of energy.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: When whole‑grain flour is used, the pretzel gains additional fiber beneficial for digestion.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cheese contains lactose, so people with intolerance should choose lactose‑free versions.

items.title: Milk‑protein allergy
items.content: Some individuals may react to the dairy proteins in the cheese topping.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Cheese toppings are often salty, which can be problematic for those with hypertension.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Cheese‑topped pretzels are calorie‑dense; portion control is recommended to avoid excess intake.

items.title: Storage requirements
items.content: Improper thawing can promote bacterial growth; pretzels should be thawed in the fridge or cooked immediately.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Thaw the pretzels in an oven (180 °C, 8‑10 min) or microwave until the cheese melts and the crust turns golden. Serve hot as a snack or with mustard, honey, or ketchup dip.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen pretzels in an airtight bag at –18 °C. Once thawed, consume within 2‑3 days when stored in the refrigerator. Do not leave at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
